title: Model a vending machine's states
description: A vending machine moves through three states: Idle (waiting for a coin), HasCoin (coin inserted, ready to dispense), and Dispensing (product is dispensing). Each state handles insertCoin(), selectProduct(), and dispense() differently. Implement the three state classes so the machine transitions correctly and rejects invalid actions.
hints: Each state class holds a reference to the VendingMachine so it can call setState()
insertCoin() in IdleState transitions to HasCoin; in HasCoin it rejects (coin already inserted)
dispense() in Dispensing transitions back to Idle after dispensing
issues: Without the State pattern, a single class with if/else chains for each state grows unmanageable
Adding a new state requires touching every action method
overallGoal: Use the State pattern to encapsulate each vending machine state in its own class, so transitions and invalid-action handling are localised.
goals: Define a State interface with a method for each action (insertCoin, ejectCoin, dispense)
Implement IdleState, HasCoinState, and DispensingState, each handling actions and transitioning the machine
Have VendingMachine delegate every action to the current State object instead of using conditionals
